item.title: 2027: Obi’s wave doesn’t exist again, he has nothing to offer — Wike
item.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has dismissed the political support behind Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying the wave that propelled him in the 2023 election no longer exists. Wike also described Obi as a dramatist, insisting that the former Anambra State governor had nothing to offer Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general election. The minister spoke on Thursday during his monthly media chat in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, where he questioned the prospects of the NDC presidential ticket featuring Obi and former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso. “All this so-called Obi kererenke doesn’t exist again. I have killed it,” Wike said. He argued that the political circumstances that helped Obi secure significant support in the 2023 presidential election had changed. “Nigerians know that Obi has nothing to offer, he is a dramatist. You were there when Soludo exposed him,” the minister said. Wike also criticised the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, saying Nigerians had already given him and other politicians opportunities to govern. “Nigerians know that Atiku and co have been given the opportunity, but they did not do anything. Nigerians know that the former governor of Rivers State looted our state,” he said. The FCT minister acknowledged Kwankwaso’s popularity but questioned whether his political influence extended beyond Kano State, where he won the 2023 presidential election. “I agree that Kwankwaso is very popular, but he ran in 2023 and won in Kano, fine, but what about the other northern states? What about the North-Central, what will happen there?” he asked. Wike further questioned whether Obi still enjoyed the level of financial and popular support associated with his 2023 presidential campaign. “The Obi wave is dead and buried. How many people are contributing money for Obi today?” he said. The post 2027: Obi’s wave doesn’t exist again, he has nothing to offer — Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Bwala to David Mark-led exco: You took over ADC leadership undemocratically and hoped all is well
item.description: Presidential aide Daniel Bwala has criticised the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), accusing it of taking over the party’s leadership without due process. Bwala made the remarks in a post on his X platform on Thursday, following the controversy surrounding the leadership of the opposition party. He said a political party seeking to govern Nigeria must uphold the principles of due process, equity and justice, accusing the Mark-led executive of disregarding those principles in its emergence. “A political party that wants to govern Nigeria must be a party of due process, equity and justice. “You descended on ADC like a thief in the night, took over its leadership undemocratically and hoped that all is well,” he wrote. Bwala further accused the leadership of violating the party’s constitution and guidelines, as well as the Nigerian Constitution and the provisions of the Electoral Act and guidelines of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). He said the alleged violations amounted to a disregard for Nigerians, accusing the party leadership of assuming that the public could be misled over the circumstances surrounding its emergence. Bwala also took a swipe at individuals lobbying on behalf of the party leadership, suggesting that they were expecting financial rewards. The comments came amid the dispute over the ADC leadership and a court ruling affecting the Mark-led executive committee. item.title: Atiku, Obi, SDP, CUPP, ADC kick as court sacks Mark-led ADC exco
item.description: By Nwafor Sunday, Henry Umoru, Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Luminous Jannamike, & John Alechelu The Federal High Court in Abuja’s decision to sack the Senator David Mark-led executive committee of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and nullify all actions taken by it has drawn criticism from former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar; Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, presidential candidate Peter Obi; the Social Democratic Party, SDP, and the Coalition of United Political Parties, CUPP. While Atiku accused the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, of using the judgment to frustrate his presidential ambition and weaken his support base in the North, Obi urged Nigerians and the judiciary to protect democratic principles and allow opposition parties to thrive. The court, in a judgment delivered on Thursday by Justice Peter Lifu , declared the Mark-led ADC caretaker committee illegal and invalidated all actions taken by it, including the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its candidate for the 2027 general election. The judgment followed a suit instituted by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the ADC (North-East), who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the party. Gombe had argued that following the resignation of the party’s former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, he was entitled to assume the leadership of the party. The court upheld his claims and granted the reliefs sought. The ruling has raised questions about the status of Atiku’s candidacy, coming barely 24 hours after he held a campaign rally in Sokoto State. Atiku alleges plot to weaken Northern support Reacting to the judgment, Atiku accused the APC of using the court ruling to frustrate his presidential ambition and contain the ADC’s growing political influence ahead of the 2027 elections. Atiku said the ruling came barely 24 hours after thousands of supporters welcomed him to Sokoto for the launch of the ADC campaign, alleging that the development was part of a strategy to weaken his Northern support base and halt the spread of his campaign beyond the region. In a statement issued on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, the former Vice-President insisted that the judgment would neither derail the party’s campaign nor diminish its appeal across the country. He said the reception in Sokoto reflected Nigerians’ growing frustration with economic hardship and their desire for a change of government. “The people of Sokoto came out in their thousands because they are hungry for change and believe in our promise to make life affordable again. What we witnessed in Sokoto is only the beginning. The people of Kebbi will have their say, and so will Nigerians across the country as our campaign moves forward,” he said. item.title: No child is useless, every child is ordained for greatness — Foluke Adeboye
item.description: By Olayinka Latona The wife of the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Foluke Adeboye, has called on parents, churches, governments and other stakeholders to take greater responsibility for raising children with godly character and values, saying Nigeria’s future depends on how its young people are nurtured. Adeboye made the call in her welcome address, titled “The Mandate of Kingdom Education in National Transformation,” at the annual summit of Christ The Redeemer’s School Management (CRSM), a multidimensional ministry of the RCCG, held at Redemption City of God along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. The summit was themed “Revisiting Kingdom Education: The Role of Stakeholders.” She said the responsibility for effective Christian education begins at home, urging parents to train their children properly and cooperate with teachers in shaping their character. Adeboye cautioned parents against over-pampering their children during school holidays, urging them to allow the young ones to grow in accordance with godly values. “Every child must fear God because the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom. We see many of these children that look down on their teachers. If parents discharge their duties effectively, it will make the teacher’s work easier. Meditate on God’s word day and night,” she said. She also urged parents not to shy away from correcting their children, stressing that discipline and proper upbringing were essential to national development. “If only everyone of us can come together, do the right things, raise our children rightly, the success of Nigeria is in our hands,” she added. Adeboye further charged children to obey their parents and called on churches to teach sound biblical doctrines. She urged leaders to discharge their responsibilities diligently and exercise sound judgment, warning that failure to provide responsible leadership could create room for corruption, criminality and other social vices. On the role of government, she called for the provision of adequate structures and learning facilities in schools, particularly in rural communities where, she said, some pupils still sit on the floor because of a lack of chairs. She noted that such schools were often upgraded through evangelism and missionary activities because of the need to address the challenges confronting rural education. “So many things are wrong and these children from the village have great destiny to fulfil. God is counting on them. They brought David from the bush to be a king of Israel. No child is a useless child; God ordained every child to be great. I believe by the time I leave, I must have made substantial impact over the education in this nation,” she said. In her keynote address on the same topic, former Minister of Education, Dr Oby Ezekwesili, said professionals who remained indifferent to the challenges facing society could not contribute meaningfully to its transformation. item.title: Tinubu saved Nigeria from turning to Venezuela — Emerhor
item.description: A founding leader of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Delta State, Olorogun O’tega Emerhor, has declared that Nigeria would have suffered an economic collapse similar to Venezuela’s if President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had not demonstrated the courage and foresight to introduce far-reaching economic reforms upon assuming office in 2023. Olorogun Emerhor, who stated this on Thursday during the Delta State APC campaign flag-off in Oleh, Isoko South Local Government Area, said Tinubu inherited an economy weakened by years of poor management and unsustainable policies, insisting that the President’s difficult but necessary decisions had rescued the country from the brink of economic disaster. The APC chieftain also called for the re-election of President Tinubu and Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, in 2027, arguing that both leaders had demonstrated the capacity to reposition the country and state for sustainable economic growth and infrastructural transformation. According to Emerhor, Nigeria was heading towards an economic crisis comparable to that of Venezuela, an oil-rich South American country that experienced severe economic difficulties despite possessing some of the world’s largest crude oil reserves. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has rescued Nigeria. If our President had not taken those bold decisions, Nigeria would have gone the way of Venezuela. Do you want Nigeria to become another Venezuela? “Venezuela has more oil than Nigeria, but bad leadership and years of economic mismanagement destroyed its economy. For many years, that was the kind of governance we experienced in Nigeria,” he stated. Emerhor criticised some opposition political figures seeking to challenge Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, alleging that several of them were part of the political establishment responsible for the country’s longstanding economic difficulties. He maintained that it took Tinubu’s political courage and determination to confront the structural challenges that previous administrations had failed to address. “All those who are today running to become President were part of the system that contributed to the destruction of Nigeria. It was Bola Ahmed Tinubu who had the courage to take those difficult decisions. “Today, we are beginning to have a stable economy. The President has laid a strong foundation for economic prosperity. We have a prudent President, and our foreign reserves are growing. Tinubu is doing well,” Emerhor declared. The APC leader argued that removing Tinubu after his first term would amount to abandoning the economic recovery process midway, stressing that the President deserved another four years to consolidate his reforms and deliver their anticipated benefits to Nigerians. item.title: ADC Judgment: CUPP accuses APC of seeking one-party state
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Coalition of United Political Parties (CUPP) has criticised the court ruling nullifying the African Democratic Congress (ADC) executive committee and its candidates, alleging that the development could weaken opposition parties and undermine political competition in Nigeria. In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday through its Office of the Spokesperson, the coalition accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of benefiting from what it described as a systematic effort to weaken opposition parties. CUPP alleged that the judgment was part of a broader attempt to undermine opposition political structures and create conditions for a one-party state. The coalition also expressed concern over the role of the judiciary, arguing that the ruling raised questions about the courts’ responsibility to protect democratic rights and political participation. The statement read in part: “CUPP views this controversial judgment not as an isolated legal dispute, but as part of a well-choreographed, state-sponsored onslaught aimed at wiping out viable opposition parties and turning Nigeria into a one-party state.” It further alleged that sections of the judiciary had failed to adequately protect the interests of citizens and the electoral process. CUPP also accused the APC-led government of relying on legal technicalities to challenge opposition candidates and party leadership structures, saying such developments could restrict political competition and undermine public confidence in the electoral system. The coalition warned that the judiciary must remain guided by the Constitution and the interests of Nigerians rather than political considerations. “The judiciary must remember that its allegiance belongs to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, not to the political actors of the day. When the courts become a tool for political liquidation, the very survival of our democracy is at stake,” the statement said. CUPP declared solidarity with the ADC and other opposition groups, saying it would continue to defend democratic participation and political pluralism. The coalition added: “CUPP stands in solidarity with the ADC and all progressive forces in Nigeria. We will not sit idly by while the hard-earned democratic gains of our nation are plundered by an authoritarian regime.” The post ADC Judgment: CUPP accuses APC of seeking one-party state appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PSC posts four commissioners of police to states
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the posting of four Commissioners of Police to Plateau, Enugu, Nasarawa and Ondo states following interviews to assess their suitability for the new assignments. The commission’s spokesman, Torty Njoku, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday at the Solomon Arase Conference Hall, PSC headquarters, Abuja. The newly posted commissioners are CP Sunday J. A. Okoebor, formerly Commissioner of Police, Police Accounts and Budget, Force Headquarters, who has been posted to Plateau State. Others are CP Fidelis Ogarabe, formerly Commissioner of Police, INTERPOL Annex, Lagos, posted to Enugu State; CP Sheikh Mohammed Danko, formerly Commissioner of Police, Force Intelligence Annex, Lagos, posted to Nasarawa State; and CP Johnson Ayodeji Babalola, formerly Commissioner of Police, Special Inquiry, Force Headquarters, Abuja, posted to Ondo State. The Chairman of the commission, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu, who affirmed the postings, said they were in line with Section 215(1)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, which empowers the commission to appoint Commissioners of Police for each state of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory. Argungu, who was represented by a board member, Hon. Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (JSC rtd.), said the officers had demonstrated the requisite knowledge and character during the interviews. He urged them to discharge their responsibilities with impartiality and live up to the expectations of their new offices. item.title: Atiku Takes Presidential Campaign To Kebbi, Pledges To Restore Fuel Subsidy
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to restore fuel subsidy, improve security and create employment if elected president in 2027. Atiku made the pledge on Thursday during a campaign rally in Kebbi State, where he called on voters to support the ADC, describing it as the only party committed to addressing the three issues. “The people of Kebbi State, let me ask you a few questions. Do you want the return of subsidy? Do you want security? Do you want employment? Therefore you have no option other than the ADC. ADC is the only political party that is committed to these three objectives and more to bring about prosperity, unity and peace to the people of our country,” he said. The former Vice President and his running mate also criticised some projects being presented as achievements of the President Bola Tinubu administration, describing them as legacies of the late President Muhammadu Buhari. Supporters of the ADC gathered at the party’s secretariat in Birnin Kebbi to welcome Atiku and other party chieftains ahead of the rally. Speaking at the event, the Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Austin Akobundu, commended party faithful for what he described as their resistance to intimidation by the state government. Akobundu said the 2027 general elections would be a referendum between suffering Nigerians and the Federal Government under President Tinubu. The ADC National Chairman, in his remarks, described the party as a moving train that no amount of intimidation could stop. He called on the people of Kebbi State to vote for Atiku as president, Abubakar Malami as governor and other ADC candidates in the 2027 general elections. The rally ended with the ADC National Chairman formally presenting the party’s flag to Malami as the party’s governorship candidate for the 2027 election. Crowd at Atiku Abubakar’s presidential campaign rally in Kebbi. The campaign in Kebbi came hours after a Federal High Court in Abuja nullified the leadership of the Senator David Mark-led ADC and voided the actions taken by the party’s executives, including the process that produced Atiku as its presidential candidate. Justice Peter Lifu delivered the judgment in a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the emergence of the Mark-led leadership. Atiku rejected the ruling, describing it as an attempt to weaken his political support and frustrate his campaign. He said he would challenge the judgment at the Court of Appeal. The ADC also rejected the decision, accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of attempting to cripple the opposition and vowing to challenge the judgment through all available judicial processes. item.title: Saudi Arabia executes five Ethiopians for hashish smuggling
item.description: Saudi Arabia has executed five Ethiopian nationals convicted of drug smuggling, bringing the kingdom’s execution toll this year to 205, according to the country’s Interior Ministry. The five were convicted of participating in smuggling hashish into the kingdom, the ministry said in a statement published by the official Saudi Press Agency on Thursday. They were executed in Asir, a province in southwestern Saudi Arabia. The latest executions are the third such announcement involving Ethiopian nationals in recent months. Five Ethiopians were executed on the same day in June, while another five were put to death in July. With the latest executions, 32 Ethiopian nationals have been executed in Saudi Arabia this year, making them the largest foreign national group among those executed. Human Rights Watch warned in July that at least 79 Ethiopians faced an imminent risk of execution over similar drug-related charges. Saudi Arabia recorded 356 executions last year, the highest annual figure in the kingdom’s history. Thousands of Ethiopians work in low-skilled jobs in Saudi Arabia, with many travelling to the oil-rich kingdom through the perilous Eastern Route from the Horn of Africa via Yemen. item.title: Atiku flags off ADC campaign in Kebbi, pledges security, fuel subsidy restoration
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi BIRNIN KEBBI — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to address Nigeria’s security challenges and restore fuel subsidy if elected president in the 2027 general elections. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), made the promises during the flag-off of his campaign in Kebbi State, where he described the forthcoming election as a referendum on the policies of the President Bola Tinubu administration. He said the election would provide Nigerians with an opportunity to decide whether to retain the current government or embrace an alternative amid concerns over economic hardship and insecurity. Supporters of the ADC converged on the party’s secretariat in Birnin Kebbi to welcome Atiku and other party chieftains ahead of the campaign rally. Speaking at the event, the Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Austin Akobundu, commended party members for attending the gathering despite what he described as intimidation by the state government. Akobundu said the 2027 election would be a referendum on the performance of the Tinubu administration, adding that hunger, insecurity and unemployment would feature prominently in the campaign. The ADC National Chairman, in his remarks, described the party as a moving train that could not be stopped by intimidation. He urged Kebbi residents to vote for Abubakar Malami as governor, Atiku as president and other ADC candidates in the 2027 elections. Atiku and his running mate also criticised some projects being presented as achievements of the Tinubu administration, alleging that they were legacies of the late President Muhammadu Buhari. They described the ADC as an alternative for Nigerians seeking improved security and a reversal of the fuel subsidy policy. The rally climaxed with the ADC National Chairman formally presenting the party’s flag to Malami as its governorship candidate for the 2027 election. Meanwhile, security was heightened in Birnin Kebbi ahead of Atiku’s arrival, with security personnel deployed across parts of the state capital to prevent any breakdown of law and order. The campaign rally ended peacefully, with no reported attacks or destruction of vehicles, unlike the violence alleged to have accompanied the party’s campaign activities in Sokoto State. item.title: Two killed, 20 abducted in Kaduna community attack
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA — Two persons have reportedly been killed and 20 others abducted after suspected terrorists invaded Akwando community in Kachia Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The attackers reportedly stormed the community around noon on Wednesday, shooting residents and abducting several people. The police had yet to officially confirm the incident as of Thursday. The President of the Kuturmi Unity Development Association (KUDA), Dr Joseph Ariko, and its Publicity Secretary, Manasseh Samuel Akwando, disclosed the attack in a statement expressing concern over the security situation in Kuturmi communities. The association said the latest attack had worsened the plight of residents still struggling to recover from previous assaults, particularly the Easter Sunday attack on Ariko community. It described the recurring incidents as a threat to the lives, livelihoods and ancestral heritage of the affected communities. KUDA identified the 20 persons reportedly abducted from Akwando as Usman Galadima, La’a’zarus Genesis, Madalin Markus, Happy Stephen, Lovet Ishaya, Afiniki Irimeya, Amina Ahmadu, Miracle Genesis, Hellen Irimeya and Musa Genesis. Others are Janet Irimeya, Gloria Markus, Zila Stephen, Alis Ahmadu, Haske Ahmadu, Great Isiac, Hanatu Irimeya, Desmon Ishaya, Siam Shagari and Nansy Genesis. The association recalled that the Easter Sunday attack on Ariko reportedly claimed five lives at the scene, while another 17 victims subsequently died in captivity. It also cited an earlier attack on Awon community, during which two persons were reportedly killed and 11 others abducted. According to KUDA, five of those abducted in Awon regained their freedom on November 3, 2026, but one reportedly died the following day. Another victim escaped, while five others allegedly died in captivity. The association said the recurring attacks had forced residents to flee their homes, abandon their farmlands and suspend economic activities for fear of further assaults. It further alleged that armed groups had restricted residents’ access to their ancestral lands, compelling some to pay levies before cultivating their farms or harvesting agricultural produce. However, KUDA said the allegations required independent investigation and urged security agencies to establish the circumstances surrounding the incidents and identify those responsible. It called on the Federal and Kaduna State governments, as well as the Kachia Local Government Council, to strengthen security in Akwando, Ariko, Awon and other vulnerable communities. Specifically, the association demanded the deployment of adequately equipped security personnel, establishment of permanent security posts, regular patrols and effective early-warning mechanisms to prevent further attacks. It also appealed for coordinated security operations to secure the release of the 20 residents reportedly abducted in Akwando and others still being held captive. item.title: Power generation drops to 3,659MW as FG explains supply disruptions
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Electricity generation on Nigeria’s national grid dropped to 3,659 megawatts (MW) as of 3pm on Thursday, from a peak of 3,996MW recorded on Wednesday, amid worsening power supply across parts of the country. The Federal Government attributed the decline to gas supply constraints to thermal power plants, reduced water inflows into hydroelectric reservoirs and operational challenges within the power sector. Data obtained from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that the decline had affected electricity allocation to Distribution Companies (DisCos), resulting in shorter hours of supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks. Data on the distribution load allocation dashboard as of 5:39pm on Thursday showed that the 11 electricity distribution companies received a combined allocation of 3,031MW. Abuja Disco received the highest allocation of 669MW, followed by Ibadan Disco with 413MW and Port Harcourt Disco with 338MW. Benin Disco received 279MW, Enugu 267MW, Eko 256MW, Ikeja 249MW, Kano 173MW, Kaduna 167MW, Jos 146MW, while Yola Disco received the lowest allocation of 74MW. The Federal Ministry of Power, in a statement on Thursday by the Special Adviser (Media and Publicity) to the Minister of Power, Adeola Adelabu, acknowledged complaints by electricity consumers in Lagos, Abuja, Ogun, Kwara and Oyo states over worsening supply in recent days. The Ministry noted that the affected areas had recently experienced noticeable improvements in electricity supply before the latest disruptions. It, however, ruled out a major or systemic failure of the national grid, explaining that preliminary assessments linked the disruptions to maintenance and operational challenges in parts of the power value chain, alongside declining generation. Acknowledging the impact of the disruptions on consumers, the Ministry said: “We recognise what every hour without power means for individuals, families and businesses, and we do not take it lightly.” It added that the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, was working with the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), NISO and electricity distribution companies to address the challenges and restore normal supply. According to the Ministry, the Minister had engaged relevant operators to resolve the operational constraints, accelerate ongoing maintenance and keep the public informed about restoration efforts. In a separate statement, NISO confirmed that limited gas availability had constrained the ability of affected thermal generating stations to operate at their available capacities, while reduced water inflows had affected hydroelectric generation. item.title: SDP condemns attempts to disqualify ADC presidential candidate, Atiku
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Social Democratic Party (SDP) has condemned alleged attempts to disqualify the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, insisting that political parties should be allowed to freely present candidates for the 2027 general elections. The party also called on the judiciary, security agencies and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remain impartial and protect the country’s democratic process. The SDP National Chairman, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, stated this on Thursday in Abuja while addressing journalists after a meeting with the party’s nine governorship candidates from different states. Gombe, who said the SDP would not participate in the proposed ‘Rainbow Coalition’, reaffirmed the party’s commitment to contesting the 2027 elections under its own political platform. He also accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of allegedly plotting to infiltrate opposition parties and weaken their ranks ahead of the elections. The SDP chairman alleged that the APC, having lost the confidence of Nigerians over its governance record, was using the proposed coalition to woo opposition members and undermine their unity. He, however, said the SDP was working with other opposition parties towards building a coalition of Nigerians committed to credible elections, including joint training of party agents and the establishment of common situation rooms to protect votes at polling units. Gombe reaffirmed the party’s commitment to presenting what he described as credible alternatives to Nigerians, particularly its presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and vice-presidential candidate, Prof. Usman Bugaje. He said: “I want to assure you that SDP, as a political party, has nothing to do with anything called Rainbow Coalition. “We are with other political parties in the opposition, doing everything possible to rescue our dear country through a coalition of the Nigerian people. “We are not into any Rainbow Coalition where we will have candidates here and profess support for the APC presidency. We are SDP and we are for SDP candidates.” He said the party had resolved to discipline any member who participated in the proposed arrangement without its authorisation. According to Gombe, the meeting with the governorship candidates was part of preparations to strengthen the party’s electoral strategies and improve its chances in the 2027 general elections. He said the engagement provided an opportunity for candidates from different states to share experiences, identify organisational gaps and develop strategies for winning elections at national and state levels. The SDP chairman urged Nigerians to assess the party’s candidates based on their competence, capacity, character and patriotism. item.title: 2027: Presidency seeks global safeguards against AI-generated falsehoods
item.description: –As Onanuga warns of threat to democratic institutions, public trust By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA–THE Presidency has called for urgent global action to check the growing misuse of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in political communication, warning that unchecked deployment of the technology could undermine democratic institutions, distort electoral processes and erode public trust ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Information and Strategy, Mr Bayo Onanuga, made the call on Thursday in Beijing, China, while delivering a paper titled, “AI and the Future of Global Communication”, at the 7th World Media Summit organised by Xinhua News Agency and the People’s Government of Beijing Municipality. Onanuga said the proliferation of AI-generated videos, images and other digital content for political purposes had made it imperative for governments, media organisations and technology stakeholders to establish safeguards against disinformation and manipulation. According to him, social media platforms, including X, Facebook and TikTok, were increasingly inundated with AI-generated content designed to advance political interests, entertain audiences and influence public opinion. With political activities and campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections gathering momentum, the presidential aide said AI had become a powerful instrument in the hands of politicians and their supporters, with the potential to serve both legitimate and destructive purposes. “We are in the thick of the political season and campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections, where new political leaders at the national and sub-national levels will be elected. AI, for good and bad, has become a powerful tool for electoral contests for politicians and their supporters. “Some political actors use AI to spread falsehoods, some use it satirically for entertainment, and some highlight candidates’ achievements,” he said. He stressed that the growing influence of AI in political communication demanded greater responsibility from political actors, media organisations and the general public, particularly in verifying information before creating, publishing or sharing digital content. While acknowledging the dangers associated with the technology, Onanuga cautioned against disregarding its enormous contributions to human development, particularly in medicine, mathematics and other areas of scientific innovation. He noted that AI had become deeply embedded in everyday life, citing its applications in vehicle safety systems, navigation and other technological solutions that had improved human efficiency and convenience. “Today, AI governs our existence, and we encounter it all the time. In the car, it warns you about your immediate surroundings. It maps your fastest route to your destination. item.title: ADC: Sokoto turnout prompted judgment voiding Atiku’s candidacy
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has alleged that the turnout at its political event in Sokoto influenced the timing of a court judgment that nullified the leadership of its David Mark-led faction and voided the party’s presidential candidacy. The party’s spokesperson, Bolaji Abdullahi, made the allegation on Channels Television’s Lunchtime Politics , while reacting to the judgment. Abdullahi said the party would challenge the ruling, insisting that the legal battle was part of what he described as sustained efforts to frustrate its political activities. He claimed that the ruling party was determined to remain in power and prevent Nigerians from having a democratic choice in the 2027 elections. “We’ve spent more time in the courts than we’ve spent on the campaign grounds, thanks to the ruling party,” he said. The ADC spokesperson alleged that the judgment was expedited following the party’s political outing in Sokoto. “But I think in the matter of hours after seeing what happened in Sokoto yesterday, the kind of reaction, the kind of turnout in Sokoto yesterday, they had to quickly go and dust up this and hurry up the judgment this morning,” Abdullahi said. He, however, said the ADC remained confident in its ability to challenge the ruling through the judicial process. “We will approach the same court. We believe in the judicial institution, regardless of the recklessness of some judges who have allowed themselves to be used as a tool for subverting democracy in Nigeria,” he said. Abdullahi said the party would apply for a stay of execution and appeal the judgment. He warned that if the ruling stood, the ADC could be prevented from fielding candidates for the presidential, governorship, National Assembly and other elections. “What is endangered is not the African Democratic Congress. What is endangered is Nigeria as a country and our democracy as we’ve known it,” he said. The ADC spokesperson maintained that the party’s message of change, affordability and improved living conditions had gained nationwide support, urging that Nigerians be allowed to choose their preferred leaders. He insisted that the judgment would not stand, adding that the party would continue its legal challenge. item.title: SDP rejects ‘Rainbow Coalition’, vows to contest 2027
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Social Democratic Party (SDP) has declared that it will participate in the 2027 general elections, distancing itself from the proposed ‘Rainbow Coalition’ and insisting that it has no intention of entering any political arrangement that could compromise its identity. The party also accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of allegedly plotting to infiltrate opposition parties and weaken their ranks ahead of the elections. The National Chairman of the SDP, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, stated these on Thursday in Abuja while addressing journalists after a marathon meeting with the party’s nine governorship candidates from different states. Gombe said the SDP had no interest in joining any arrangement that would compromise its political identity or align its candidates with the ruling party. He alleged that the APC, having lost public confidence over its governance record, was using the proposed coalition to woo opposition members and undermine the unity of other political parties. The chairman, however, said the SDP was working with other opposition parties towards building a coalition of Nigerians committed to credible elections, including joint training of party agents and the establishment of common situation rooms to protect votes at polling units. He reaffirmed the party’s commitment to presenting what he described as credible alternatives to Nigerians, particularly its presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and running mate, Prof. Usman Bugaje. Gombe said: “I want to assure you that SDP, as a political party, has nothing to do with anything called Rainbow Coalition. “We are with other political parties in the opposition, doing everything possible to rescue our dear country through a coalition of the Nigerian people. “We are not into any Rainbow Coalition where we will have candidates here and profess support for the APC presidency. We are SDP and we are for SDP candidates.” He said the party had also resolved to discipline any member who participated in the proposed arrangement without its authorisation. According to him, the meeting with the governorship candidates was part of preparations to strengthen the party’s electoral strategies and improve its chances in the 2027 general elections. He said the engagement provided an opportunity for candidates from different states to share experiences, identify organisational gaps and develop strategies for winning elections at national and state levels. Gombe urged Nigerians to assess the party’s candidates based on their competence, capacity, character and patriotism. He also pledged the SDP’s commitment to credible elections, saying it would collaborate with other opposition parties on election monitoring, training of polling agents and the establishment of joint situation rooms. “We will be our own INEC at the polling units and our own security to ensure free, fair and credible elections come 2027,” he said. item.title: Tinubu Congratulates Flamingos, Backs Team To Win U-17 World Cup
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, on their 3-1 victory over Brazil in Wednesday’s semi-final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. In a statement issued by his media aide, Bayo Onanuga, the President described the team’s qualification for the final as a remarkable achievement that has brought immense pride and joy to millions of Nigerians at home and abroad. Tinubu also commended the coaching crew and everyone whose hard work and support contributed to the team’s successful campaign. As the Flamingos prepare to face Japan in the final, the President urged the players to remain focused, confident and determined, assuring them of the prayers, goodwill and unwavering support of Nigerians. “I encourage you to approach the final with the same fighting spirit and belief that have brought you this far. I have confidence in your ability to make history by winning the coveted world title. “I call on all Nigerians to rally behind the young ambassadors of the nation, whose achievements continue to showcase Nigeria’s sporting excellence and inspire a new generation of girls to pursue their dreams uninhibited. “Once again, Nigeria is proud of you. Go for the trophy, Flamingos!” he added. President Bola Tinubu The Flamingos reached the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup for the first time after defeating Brazil 3-1 in their semi-final encounter in Morocco. The Nigerian girls produced a spirited second-half performance, scoring three goals before Brazil grabbed a late consolation. Queen Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute, finishing off an assist from Oluwakemi Adegubyi to give Nigeria the lead. The Flamingos doubled their advantage in the 71st minute when Awawu Bashiru found the net, with Joseph providing the assist. Bashiru struck again in the 80th minute to make it 3-0, converting a pass from Oluebube Umejiaku as Nigeria took firm control of the encounter. Brazil pulled one back in the 89th minute through Greise Kelly, assisted by Yasmin Queiroz, but the goal came too late to prevent Nigeria from securing victory and a place in the final. item.title: France Workers Strike, March For ‘Dignified Wage’
item.description: Striking workers marched across France against the rising cost of living on Thursday, with hundreds of thousands of people expected to take to the streets nationwide in a new escalation following weeks of protest. More than 250,000 people were taking part in demonstrations across 73 cities by the afternoon, the major labour union CGT said. The demonstrations come as the eurozone’s second largest economy battles to redress its finances, six months ahead of elections to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in opinion polls. The high school student movement that began with youths protesting over learning conditions has coincided with widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, which culminated on October 17 in the worst rioting France has seen in years. Sylvie Larneury, 61, a healthcare manager, and her 61-year-old partner, an IT specialist, were on strike Thursday so they could join the march in the central city of Clermont-Ferrand. “We’re fed up. We’re not starving, but we have to help our children even though they’ve studied,” she said. “We’ve had enough of social injustice,” she added, criticising what she called “a repressive government that defends its own interests and not those of the majority”. The unions are calling for across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people and have complained about police restrictions on certain protests. Protesters take part in a demonstration as part of a nationwide day of actions as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks in Bordeaux on November 5, 2026. Photo by CHRISTOPHE ARCHAMBAULT / AFP Protesting in the city of Lyon, winegrower Martin Thiberge said he wanted to take part in demonstrations he saw as drawing together people from across French society. “We want to make a living from our work, to make a dignified wage,” he said. As many as 80,000 people were expected to march from 2:00 pm (1300 GMT) in the capital Paris. The planned action prompted the Eiffel Tower to close for the day, operators said on the monument’s website. School blockades Dozens of high-schoolers protested in several cities, with the government reporting blockades at 81 out of the country’s 3,700 high schools. A high school student association said classes had been suspended at 1,000 such secondary schools, including those blockaded and those closed on a day of strikes. Around 16 percent of teachers nationwide were on strike, the education ministry said. In Paris, police used tear gas to try to prevent students from blocking access to the Helene-Boucher high school, an AFP reporter said. item.title: ‘Why We Should Continue To Support Tinubu’, Wike To Nigerians
item.description: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, has explained the many reasons Nigerians should re-elect President Bola Tinubu in the upcoming 2027 general elections. The FCT Minister spoke on Wednesday during his monthly ministerial press briefing in Port Harcourt on Thursday. Wike said he enjoyed his job as FCT Minister and remained committed to it. “I enjoy my job as FCT Minister, and I’m committed to it. Yes, I have pressure to deliver, but positively,” he said. Wike also said Ogoni people had benefited from empowerment under the President. “Ogoni people have been looking for empowerment, and now President Tinubu has done a lot of empowerment for them. If you tell them not to vote for Mr President, they’ll look at you like you’re not okay,” he said. He insisted that “no government has done more in the fight against insecurity than this government.” The former Rivers State governor responded to critics and political rivals, including the Turaki-led PDP faction, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodinma, and the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), University of Abuja branch. Up till now I still have mosquito bites,” he said. He added: “You budgeted $39m to construct a general hospital and up till now we can’t find any hospital. How can I support such a person? He sold out gas turbine, so what’s the impact of his leadership on Rivers people?” Wike further alleged that Amaechi contracted a Ghanaian to plant trees along Aba Road for N8bn. “My brother, it was terrible!
